explain.say: After a terrible war, how do you stop the next one? In 1945 world leaders tried something new: a club where nearly every country could talk instead of fight. It is the United Nations. The timeline shows how it was born.

faq.a: A statement made in August 1941 by US President Franklin Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, setting out hopes for the world after the war, like self-government and lasting peace. It inspired the United Nations.
asks: How did the idea of the UN begin?

faq.a: Delegates from 50 countries at the San Francisco Conference, from April to June 1945. Poland signed soon after, making 51 founding members. The Charter sets out the UN's aims and rules.

faq.q: When was the United Nations founded?
faq.a: On 24 October 1945, when its Charter came into force. That date is celebrated every year as United Nations Day.

faq.q: What is the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
faq.a: A document adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948. It lists 30 rights every person should have, like freedom from slavery, education and fair trials. Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the committee that drafted it.

faq.q: What does the Security Council do?
faq.a: It is responsible for keeping international peace. It has 15 members, and five permanent members, China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States, can veto its decisions. Many people argue it should be reformed.

facts: The United Nations Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.
The United Nations has 193 member states.
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted on 10 December 1948.
